Built on meritocracy, our unique company culture rewards self-starters and those who are committed to doing what is best for our customers.

Brown & Brown is seeking a Senior Vice President, IT Strategy & Innovation to join our growing team! This role offers a hybrid work arrangement and can be based out of our offices in Plano, Charlotte, Maryland, Washington, DC, or Virginia.

The Senior Vice President of IT Strategy & Innovation is a visionary technology executive responsible for shaping the long-term technology direction of the enterprise while driving near-term innovation and incubation. This leader will define and execute an integrated IT strategy aligned with corporate objectives, advance enterprise architecture, and champion innovation with a strong emphasis on data, AI, and interoperability. As a direct report to the CITO, this role influences the entire technology landscape and plays a critical part in enabling business growth through modern, scalable, and forward-thinking solutions.

How You Will Contribute:

- Develop and maintain a comprehensive, multi-year IT strategy that is tightly aligned with the company's business vision, priorities, and growth objectives.
- Ensure technology strategy directly enables business outcomes, operational excellence, and competitive differentiation.
- Lead the enterprise innovation agenda, with a strong focus on AI, automation, data-driven capabilities, and next-generation digital experiences.
- Balance long-term strategic planning with agile, iterative incubation efforts that accelerate value creation.
- Oversee the Enterprise Architecture function, ensuring cohesive architectural standards, frameworks, and policies across the organization.
- Establish and maintain architectural guidelines that promote interoperability, scalability, security, and modernization.
- Partner with technology and business leaders to ensure architectural decisions support business outcomes and future-state capabilities.
- Identify, evaluate, and incubate emerging technologies—especially in AI, data platforms, and integration ecosystems—to drive competitive advantage.
- Build and lead innovation programs, labs, and pilots that rapidly test, validate, and prove value for new concepts.
- Foster a culture of experimentation, continuous learning, and responsible innovation.
- Lead, mentor, and inspire a diverse team of technologists, architects, and innovators across the enterprise.
- Build organizational capability in AI, data engineering, architecture, and modern technology practices.
- Champion career development, technical excellence, and a culture of collaboration and empowerment.
- Serve as a brilliant communicator who can translate complex technology concepts into clear, compelling narratives for all audiences—from engineers to the Board.
- Partner closely with business leaders to co-create technology-enabled strategies that drive growth, efficiency, and transformation.
- Represent IT Strategy & Innovation in executive forums, steering committees, and cross-functional initiatives.

Skills & Experience to be Successful:

- 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in technology strategy, enterprise architecture, innovation, or related domains.
- Deep expertise in data platforms, AI/ML, interoperability, and modern integration patterns.
- Proven track record of developing and executing enterprise-level technology strategies.
- Demonstrated success leading innovation programs and incubating emerging technologies.
- Exceptional people leader with a passion for developing high-performing teams and nurturing technical talent.
- Outstanding communicator capable of engaging technical and non-technical audiences with clarity, confidence, and influence.
- Strong collaborator who builds trusted relationships across business and technology functions.
- Strategic thinker with the ability to operate at both 30,000 feet and ground level.
- Comfortable navigating ambiguity, driving change, and making bold decisions.
- Entrepreneurial spirit with a bias for action and a commitment to delivering measurable outcomes.

# Brown & Brown (NYSE:BRO) - Senior Vice President, IT Strategy & Innovation briefing packet
| Senior Vice President, IT Strategy & Innovation | Not provided | Reports to CITO (enterprise technology strategy) |

## JD Complement
The role sits at the intersection of a large, acquisition-driven insurance intermediary and a modern enterprise technology agenda. The operating tension is not “build a product,” but “standardize enough to scale while preserving the local,
producer-led model that drives growth.”

Brown & Brown’s context implies this leader must translate a decentralized business into a more interoperable technology estate without slowing the pace of acquisitions, teammate productivity, or client service.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Brown & Brown is a regulated insurance brokerage and risk intermediary, not a software company. It wins through distribution, relationships, specialty expertise, and disciplined M&A, with growth amplified by a long-running producer-led
culture.

The archetype is hybrid: services-led with strong partner/channel economics and a platform-like need for shared data, workflow, and governance across many businesses. The central tension is local autonomy versus enterprise consistency.

The company’s culture language emphasizes meritocracy and self-starters, which usually means influence is earned through execution, not central mandate. For technology, that often creates a need for pragmatic standards, not heavy-handed
transformation theater.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Brown & Brown was founded in 1939 and has grown into one of the largest insurance brokerages in the world, with over 23,000 teammates worldwide. It is publicly traded on the NYSE under BRO and operates under the scrutiny of investors who
expect durable organic growth plus acquisition integration.

A major strategic pressure is scale management: every acquisition adds books of business, systems, data, and operating variation. The technology strategy role likely exists to reduce integration friction, improve decision rights, and make
enterprise capabilities reusable across a growing footprint.

The company’s recent acquisition activity, including the announced agreement to acquire Accession Risk Management Group in 2025, reinforces the need for architecture that can absorb growth without creating a brittle core.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Verified top leadership includes J. Powell Brown as President and Chief Executive Officer and R. Andrew Watts as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.
Officer function, which is the likely direct operating partner for this role.

The stakeholder map likely spans:
- Executive leadership focused on growth, margin, and acquisition integration
- Business unit leaders who protect local speed and client intimacy
- Risk, compliance, and privacy functions given the regulated environment
- Data, architecture, and application leaders who must harmonize standards across businesses
- M&A and integration teams that need repeatable onboarding patterns

This role likely needs credibility with both corporate leadership and operating leaders who may resist centralization if it slows revenue production.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Brown & Brown has publicly signaled interest in AI and innovation, including content on AI risk and a 2026 AI-first enterprise direction reported alongside broader enablement efforts. That suggests the company is moving from curiosity to
enterprise adoption.

For this role, the important signal is not model research; it is enterprise readiness:
- Data quality and interoperability across acquired businesses
- Architecture standards that support reuse without over-standardizing the field
- AI enablement that improves teammate productivity and client responsiveness
- Integration patterns that can connect legacy and modern systems
- Governance that keeps innovation aligned with privacy, compliance, and operational controls

The likely architecture challenge is to create a common enterprise backbone while preserving enough flexibility for specialty practices and local operating models.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Brown & Brown is not primarily a technology ecosystem company, but it is deeply partner-dependent in its core business model. Its external motion is built around carrier relationships, client advisory, and acquisition partnerships rather
than software alliances.

For this role, ecosystem relevance is internal and operational: the company likely needs vendor, implementation, and advisory partners to accelerate AI, data, and architecture modernization. The key motion is not marketplace revenue; it is
technical close through trusted execution partners.

## Recent Events & Urgency
The company’s 2025 acquisition announcement and continued investor-relations activity point to ongoing scale pressure. In a business like Brown & Brown, growth creates urgency around integration speed, data consistency, and enterprise
controls.

The broader insurance brokerage market also remains competitive on talent, specialty expertise, and acquisition discipline. That raises the bar for technology leaders who can make the enterprise easier to run without diluting the
entrepreneurial culture.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise strategy in a regulated, acquisition-heavy environment
- Operating model simplification across decentralized business units
- Architecture governance that enables scale without slowing producers
- Data interoperability and integration across heterogeneous systems
- AI adoption framed as productivity, service, and control
- Change leadership in a culture that values autonomy and merit
- Executive communication across business, risk, and technology audiences

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Reference the challenge of scaling a broker platform through acquisitions without losing local speed
- Speak to enterprise architecture as a way to reduce integration drag and improve teammate productivity
- Mention AI as an enablement layer for producers, service teams, and operations, not as a lab exercise
- Tie data interoperability to faster onboarding of acquired businesses and cleaner decision-making
- Acknowledge the need to balance central standards with Brown & Brown’s entrepreneurial culture
- Position innovation as practical modernization that supports growth, compliance, and client service

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume/proof graph, not from this packet.
